claim: The database serialises what the code must not guess: an idempotency key is a unique-index claim, a job is a row claimed under a lock, a race has one winner and the losers are told what it did.
A state machine is one table that the code and the database share; a trigger refuses the edge the table does not list, and a test fails when the two copies drift.
An unknown outcome is a result, not a failure: a timeout or a 5xx licenses neither retry nor failover until a read proves what happened.
At-least-once delivery is stated, not hidden: the claim is committed before the network call and the receiver is told to deduplicate.
Each process connects to the database as a role that can do only what it needs, granted after the migrations run and revoked on everything else.
A layer boundary is enforced by tooling or it is only a belief: lint rules and dependency rules decide what a domain module may import.
Slow or unreliable third-party work leaves the request path: the request records what was asked and answers, and a worker does the rest.
Reproduce a failure before fixing it, with a harness that runs the real dependency or a stub that copies its awkwardness.
Reports read a read model, not the collection the workers write on every run.
Every claim about a system on this site links to the file and line that prove it, at a commit the build verifies.
